scenes.heading: Data Lake
scenes.subheading: Store everything now, structure it later
scenes.narration: A data lake is a storage system that holds vast amounts of raw data in its native format until it is needed.

scenes.heading: What defines a data lake
bullets: Stores raw data in any format
Handles structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data
Applies schema on read, not on write
scenes.narration: A data lake stores raw data in whatever format it arrives, without forcing a schema upfront. It can hold structured tables, semi-structured JSON, and unstructured files all together. It applies schema on read, meaning structure is imposed only when the data is queried. And it typically uses cheap, scalable object storage, so keeping everything is affordable.

scenes.heading: Warehouse vs lake
scenes.narration: A warehouse holds structured, modeled data with a schema enforced when data is written, ideal for SQL analytics. A lake holds raw data of any format and imposes schema only when read, offering flexibility for diverse uses. Many organizations use both, feeding curated data from the lake into the warehouse.

scenes.text: A data lake stores raw data of any type cheaply, deferring structure until you actually need it.
scenes.narration: The key point is that a data lake cheaply stores raw data of every type and defers structure until the moment you actually query it.
